correctness.rationale: Orthogonality identifies all ordered-pair fibers. At nonzero a, the derivative kernel of the Gold polynomial is a F_{2^gcd(m,k)} additive line, making every nonempty fiber exactly s. Three Cauchy inequalities give the sharp 1+s(1-1/q) bound, with equality attained at f=1. An exact nonnegative deficit identity reconstructs every equality constraint and proves the subfield-line-affine sign characterization. A standalone exact checker tests 21 field/exponent cases and four direct Fourier sums. The infinite family is established analytically, not by enumeration.

value.rationale: The nonlinear Gold graphs are natural benchmark objects in finite-field harmonic analysis and differential uniformity. The exact sharp weighted Fourier fourth moment depends on gcd(m,k), and the necessary-and-sufficient phase characterization exhibits a real jump from arbitrary signs in the APN case to subfield-line-affine signs for larger gcd. The explicit nonlinear quadratic phases and exact three-channel deficit give meaningful structure beyond redisplaying a known differential spectrum; the result requires no downstream theorem to motivate this canonical sharp endpoint.
